    \caption{Top-1 accuracy (\%) in the continual setting on ImageNet-C, severity 5, per corruption. Large / small: ViT-B/16 / ResNet-50 (V1), adapted with TENT, severity 5. The stream concatenates the 15 corruptions in CoTTA's standard order, 50000 images per corruption, with no reset: the models adapt continually from the source weights. The duos combine the models as $(z_L / T_L + z_S / T_S) / 2$ with $T_L = 0.65$, $T_S = 1.01$, fitted on the four held-out corruptions pooled, on the frozen models' logits. \emph{Frozen duo}: no adaptation. \emph{Fixed TS duo}: the models adapt on their own entropy. Vanilla DD and Joint DD weight the members with $w_L = \sigma(\beta (s_L - s_S))$, $s$ the logit of the nnn proxy (identity calibration, no temporal filter) computed on proxy batches of 256 samples, $\beta = 0.5$, and pool the logits as $w_L z_L / T_L + w_S z_S / T_S$ with $w_S = 1 - w_L$. In Vanilla DD the gate sits outside the adaptation loop (the members adapt on their own entropy and never see it); in Joint DD it sits inside, and both members adapt on the entropy of the gated prediction. Any model that does not adapt is frozen: it keeps its weights and uses the test batch's normalization statistics. Hyperparameters of the adapting models: batch size 64. The optimizer depends on the entropy the models minimize. Models that adapt on their own entropy: ViT-B/16: SGD (learning rate $7 \times 10^{-5}$, momentum 0.9, dampening 0, weight decay 0, no Nesterov). ResNet-50 (V1): SGD (learning rate $5 \times 10^{-4}$, momentum 0.9, dampening 0, weight decay 0, no Nesterov). Models that adapt on the duo entropy: ViT-B/16: SGD (learning rate $3.2 \times 10^{-3}$, momentum 0.9, dampening 0, weight decay 0, no Nesterov). ResNet-50 (V1): SGD (learning rate $4 \times 10^{-3}$, momentum 0.9, dampening 0, weight decay 0, no Nesterov). With one model adapting on the duo entropy, it uses its optimizer from this list. The own-entropy rows (Fixed TS duo, Vanilla DD) use the first set of learning rates, Joint DD the second.}
